label: Timer callback
type: the fourth Eventing Function entry point: the JavaScript function invoked when a createTimer() Timer matures/fires. A member of eventing-handler-family. Addressed by source pages under two different predicates depending on framing - firesCallback (eventing:timer -firesCallback-> this, from the Timer's own perspective) and hasHandler (eventing:function -hasHandler-> this, from the Function's declared-entry-points perspective) - both are kept, deliberately, rather than forcing one.
aliases_note: Folds two independently-minted, non-variant, same-prefix ids describing one mechanism: eventing:timer-callback (10 files, minted via firesCallback, from the worked-example/handler pages that demonstrate a Timer actually firing) and eventing:timer-callback-handler (6 files, minted via hasHandler, from eventing-Terminologies.md/eventing-language-constructs.md/eventing-timers.md, which state the entry-point list). Zero file overlap - 16 distinct files total, spanning both code-sample pages and reference/terminology pages, which is a genuinely stronger independence signal than a duplicate pair. Neither recurrence.py --variants nor --forks catches this kind of fork; see the family record's note.
evidence: The Eventing Service calls the OnUpdate, OnDelete, and Timer Callback handlers on mutations and fired timers.
When a Timer created by the Eventing Function fires, the callback `DocTimerCallback` executes and writes a new document in the target collection.
Re-executes the timer ASAP to ensure the Timer keeps running in case errors or script timeouts happen in later "recurring work".
relates_to_competency_question: What runs when a scheduled Timer fires, and is that a different kind of entry point from OnUpdate/OnDelete?
